title: POC Weekly Sync - App Integration: SDK, Tool/Function Calls, Structured Output
summary: Weekly POC sync to review integration progress for Redwood SDK into VenturePay's payments app. Covered SDK auth, function/tool calling for payments workflow, structured invoice output, latency/batching tradeoffs, and security questions (VPC/KMS/SOC2). Agreed next steps: send benchmark results, security pack, and schedule infra deep-dive next week.
topics: Tool/function call patterns for payments flow
Structured output for invoice extraction and routing
next_steps: Redwood to share 95th pct latency benchmark on our model variant by 2026-03-02
Redwood SE to send security whitepaper + SOC2 summary by 2026-03-01
VenturePay to run SDK end-to-end smoke test and share logs by 2026-03-05
action_items: Evan Li: run SDK end-to-end test with sample invoice dataset and upload logs (due 2026-03-05)
Diego Alvarez: export latency/batching tuning notes and share config snippet (due 2026-03-02)
Maya Chen: send security pack (SOC2, KMS integration notes) and pricing draft (due 2026-03-01)
Sasha Patel: confirm success criteria for structured output (schema + edge cases) (due 2026-03-04)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we know you have a packed day, this is our weekly poc sync for venturepay integration. i have diego from se with me.
[00:08] Priya Rao: cool, thanks maya. Priya here. we'll probably start with a quick status update from our side.
[00:14] Evan Li: yeah, quick note — we ran the SDK sample yesterday, auth worked but saw some 401s intermittently when token rotated, still debugging, maybe something on our refresh logic.
[00:24] Diego Alvarez: okay noted, Evan — are you using the client credential flow from the latest SDK? there was a bug fixed in 0.9.4 around token caching.
[00:31] Evan Li: we pulled 0.9.3, that explains it. we'll upgrade.
[00:35] Maya Chen: perfect, that should likely resolve the 401s. also we'll send a tiny snippet that shows recommended refresh pattern.
[00:42] Sasha Patel: on the product side, we validated the structured output example you sent, one comment: the invoice schema needs a separate "line_items" array with tax fields, the sample flattened it and our backend ETL choked.
[00:55] Diego Alvarez: thanks — we can extend the structured-output template. question: do you want strict JSON schema enforcement or a best-effort parsing with validation hooks?
[01:05] Priya Rao: leaning strict for downstream systems, but we also need fallback for OCR fuzziness. maybe schema validation plus a confidence score per field.
[01:14] Maya Chen: makes sense — Redwood's structured output can emit confidence meta per field. we'll add that to the template and include line_items + tax.
[01:23] Evan Li: great. on performance, we ran a small batch of 50 invoices via hosted endpoint, median latency looked fine ~220ms, but p95 spiked to 1.2s under concurrent load of 10 rps.
[01:36] Diego Alvarez: two levers: batching and model variant. for real-time payment flows I'd recommend smaller batch sizes and the faster 8-bit quantized variant; for high-throughput nightly jobs use batching and cache. Did you test with kv cache enabled?
[01:48] Evan Li: not yet. we hit tokenization differences as well; our prompt has a 1k context window with long receipts.
[01:56] Diego Alvarez: that will amplify kernel selection; we'll share recommended kernel/config and a quantization profile. fast variant reduces p95 but may slightly increase token hallucination; we'll show tradeoffs on sample evals.
[02:11] Priya Rao: security: product people flagged KMS integration — can Redwood private deploy integrate with our AWS KMS?
[02:19] Maya Chen: yes, private and dedicated can integrate with your KMS/HSM. for hosted we use envelope encryption and we offer customer-managed key options with FIPS modules on dedicated/private. we'll include integration notes in the security pack.
[02:32] Sasha Patel: any SOC2 stuff we should be aware of for vendor due diligence?
[02:36] Maya Chen: we are SOC2 Type II, will send the attestation. also provide audit logs, SSO/SAML guide, and RBAC docs.
[02:46] Evan Li: nice. on tool/function calling — our payments flow needs a function call that returns parsed invoice + routing decision (e.g., auto-settle, manual review) and a confidence score. how does Redwood handle function returns and deterministic routing?
[02:59] Diego Alvarez: two approaches: 1) use SDK function-call API where model returns structured JSON and Redwood enforces response schema; or 2) run model -> output -> post-processor lambda. Using function calls with structured output reduces glue code and we can attach validation hooks. You can also configure routing policy: if confidence < threshold forward to manual queue.
[03:19] Priya Rao: are there examples for async retries? in our pipeline we need idempotent retries when downstream services time out.
[03:27] Diego Alvarez: yes, we have a retry pattern in the SDK sample: use idempotency_key and the SDK's request status endpoint. we'll share that snippet.
[03:35] Sasha Patel: latency SLOs — we're targeting 500ms p95 for checkout flows; is that realistic on hosted?
[03:43] Diego Alvarez: hosted can hit that with the faster variant and small batch size for low concurrency. if you need strict SLOs at scale, Dedicated with reserved GPUs gives more predictable p95. We can run an SLA benchmark during the pilot.
[03:58] Evan Li: cost is a consideration — dedicated looks expensive but predictable. any rough monthly estimate for our projected 2 million transactions?
[04:07] Maya Chen: rough ballpark — we'll provide a pricing draft. Dedicated has commit tiers; sometimes hybrid routing (hosted for burst, dedicated for steady) is cost-effective. we'll model it in the pricing doc.
[04:19] Priya Rao: good. on observability, can we get per-token cost / trace to customer request ID?
[04:26] Diego Alvarez: yes, Redwood Console exposes token cost breakdown per request and you can pass correlation_id in the SDK for traceability.
[04:34] Sasha Patel: a couple of dev questions: does the SDK support Node and Python and does it support serverless environments?
[04:41] Maya Chen: yes to both. node/python SDKs and lightweight clients for serverless. we recommend the streaming API for UI flows.
[04:49] Evan Li: we tried the streaming edge but hit some chunking issues with our websocket impl. likely our client lib.
[04:55] Diego Alvarez: we have a troubleshooting guide for streaming; will include a websocket sample.
[05:00] Priya Rao: one more — data residency. some european merchants require data residency in eu-west-1, do you support region pinning?
[05:09] Maya Chen: yes, region routing and customer tenancy can be configured; private deployments allow full control. Hosted supports region pinning in most regions.
[05:17] Sasha Patel: ok next steps recap?
[05:20] Maya Chen: quick recap — redwood to send benchmark results (p95/p50), security pack, SDK snippets for token refresh, streaming troubleshooting, function-call schema with confidence meta, and a pricing draft. VenturePay to run SDK tests and confirm schema edge cases. schedule infra deep-dive for next week.
[05:38] Evan Li: sounds good. I'll log the SDK test action item.
[05:41] Priya Rao: thanks all, that was helpful.
[05:44] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts. bye.
[05:48] [meeting end]
